summary: Grace writes short, dense asks that define "done" before any work starts — usually a countable condition plus a doc note, so the fix teaches the codebase something. She refuses the easy workaround by name (no retry bumps, no buffer-it-in-memory) and makes the agent root-cause instead. Research requests come with an output format and bounded depth, which turns "look into it" into a deliverable. Threads stay short: one task per session, re-briefed cheaply, with a quick nudge the moment the agent drifts from the constraint that matters.

traits.title: Defines "done" before the work starts
traits.detail: Tasks end with a countable condition, not a feeling — and often a one-line doc note so the lesson sticks.

evidence.quote: Done means: retries removed, suite green 20 consecutive runs (`npm run test:loop 20`), and a short note in TESTING.md about the timer rule.

traits.title: Root-causes instead of papering over
traits.detail: Names the tempting workaround and forbids it, so the agent digs for the shared underlying cause.

evidence.quote: Root-cause each one instead of bumping retries — they share a leaked fake-timer pattern.

traits.title: Research asks carry an output format
traits.detail: Comparisons specify the columns, the sources and the decision they feed, which bounds the depth automatically.

evidence.quote: Output: a one-page table (throughput, replay, ops burden, our-stack fit) + your recommendation with the single strongest reason and the single biggest risk.

traits.title: States the constraint that will bite
traits.detail: Acceptance criteria include the resource limit or scale that would otherwise surface in production.

evidence.quote: Accept: a 500k-row export completes without the node process exceeding 300MB RSS.

traits.title: One task, one session
traits.detail: Starts fresh per task instead of dragging stale context; short threads keep the model on the current constraint.

evidence.quote: new session for the export work — the flaky-test context doesn't apply here

templates.title: Say what done means
templates.prompt: <task> in <project> (search "<marker>" to find the spots). Root-cause instead of <the easy workaround>. Done means: <the workaround removed>, <suite> green <N> consecutive runs (`<command>`), and a short note in <doc> about <the rule>.

templates.title: Research with a deliverable
templates.trait: Research asks carry an output format
templates.prompt: Before we pick <choice> for <project>: compare <option A> vs <option B> for our workload (<the numbers that matter>). Read the actual docs, not blog posts. Output: a one-page table (<columns>) + your recommendation with the single strongest reason and the single biggest risk.

templates.title: Acceptance with a resource limit
templates.trait: States the constraint that will bite
templates.prompt: Add <feature> to <project>. Reuse <existing mechanism> so <it stays consistent>. <The perf approach — stream, don't buffer>. Accept: <the large case> completes without <process> exceeding <limit>.
